items.question: What fate regarding death and splendor awaits the accomplished practitioner?
premises: Death does not occur for him
His splendor is imperishable
His splendor is immortal
items.inference: The practitioner becomes free from death and possesses imperishable immortal splendor
items.plain_english: For him there is no death; indeed his splendor is imperishable and immortal.

items.question: What power does an angered accomplished practitioner wield over the three worlds?
premises: The practitioner can become angered
He has the power to shake
The three worlds include moving and unmoving beings
items.inference: When angered, the practitioner can shake the entire three worlds with all moving and unmoving beings
items.plain_english: But when angered, O goddess, he can shake the three worlds with all that moves and does not move.

items.question: What determines the kind of accomplishment attained by the practitioner?
premises: Accomplishment arises in a certain manner
Constant practice is the means
Practice alone brings about the result
items.inference: The nature of accomplishment depends entirely on constant practice
items.plain_english: And whatever kind of accomplishment arises comes indeed from constant practice.

items.question: How is this supreme knowledge characterized in relation to autonomy and accomplishment?
premises: This is knowledge
It is supreme knowledge
It is oriented toward autonomy and accomplishment
items.inference: This knowledge is the supreme knowledge consisting in the mind of autonomy and accomplishment
uncertainties: The exact syntactic relation of svātantra+siddhi+mānasī to jñānaṃ is slightly compressed
items.plain_english: This knowledge is the supreme knowledge, the mind of autonomy and accomplishment.

items.question: Who should receive this knowledge and with what attitude in the Kaula path?
premises: This knowledge must be taken
It requires effort
The recipient desires accomplishment in the Kaula path
items.inference: One who desires accomplishment in the Kaula path should receive this knowledge with effort
items.plain_english: One who desires accomplishment in the Kaula path should take this up with effort.

items.question: What physical and mental technique should the practitioner perform with the tongue and mind?
premises: The tongue should be turned upward
The mind should be fixed there
These actions are prescribed
items.inference: The practitioner should turn the tongue upward and fix the mind in that place
uncertainties: The exact referent of tasmin is context-dependent
items.plain_english: Having turned the tongue upward, one should fix the mind there.

items.question: What afflictions are removed from the practitioner through this technique?
premises: Freedom occurs in a moment
The practitioner is freed from diseases
These include illness, death, old age, and others
items.inference: Through this practice one is quickly freed from diseases, illness, death, old age, and similar afflictions
items.plain_english: In a moment one is freed from diseases, from illness, death, old age, and the like.

items.question: What specific healing effect occurs in relation to pungent experience and disease?
premises: Disease is destroyed in a moment
A pungent experience is involved
Leprosy is destroyed
items.inference: In a moment disease is destroyed, and in the pungent state there is destruction of leprosy
uncertainties: The precise meaning of kaṭuke in this yogic context is ambiguous
items.plain_english: In a moment disease is destroyed; in the pungent experience there is the destruction of leprosy.

items.question: What qualities does a person gain through experiencing the taste of milk?
premises: The taste of milk is experienced
The person becomes wise
The person becomes immortal
items.inference: By the taste of milk, a person becomes wise and immortal
uncertainties: kṣīra+svādena may refer to a yogic nectar rather than literal milk
items.plain_english: By the taste of milk, a person becomes wise and immortal.

items.question: Where should the mind be placed to produce the yogic yawning effect?
premises: The mind should be placed in the circle
The mind should be placed in the nose
Yawning arises in this context
items.inference: Placing the mind in the circle and in the nose produces the yawning state
uncertainties: The exact technical meaning of cakreṇa and vijṛmbhikā is unclear
items.plain_english: One should place the mind in the circle and in the nose; then yawning arises.

items.question: What kinds of divine beings or states may the practitioner attain through this practice?
premises: Divine maidens of the gods are involved
Yakṣas and Vidyādharas are mentioned
Such a state may come to be
items.inference: The practitioner may attain association with divine maidens and become like a Yakṣa or Vidyādhara
uncertainties: The syntax is compressed and the exact subject of bhavet is ambiguous
items.plain_english: He may become associated with divine maidens of the gods and become like a Yakṣa or Vidyādhara.

items.question: What enjoyment results from attracting many divine maidens, O beloved?
premises: Many divine maidens are attracted
Attraction precedes enjoyment
Enjoyment follows as a result
items.inference: Having attracted many divine maidens, they enjoy them, O beloved
uncertainties: The subject of bhuñjate is not explicitly stated
items.plain_english: Having attracted many divine maidens, they enjoy them, O beloved.

items.question: What distinguishes a true yogin in terms of upward-retained seminal energy?
premises: A yogin becomes one of upward-retained semen
A mere yogin by hand is negated
The distinction is addressed to the beloved
items.inference: The true yogin is one whose seminal energy flows upward, not one defined by manual practice alone
uncertainties: The token karata(? is corrupt or uncertain in the source
items.plain_english: The yogin becomes one whose energy flows upward; he is not a yogin merely by hand, O beloved.

items.question: How rare and supreme is this circle compared to other yogic practices?
premises: This circle is difficult to obtain
No yoga is higher than this
It is presented as supreme
items.inference: This circle is rare and there is no yoga higher than it
items.plain_english: This circle is indeed difficult to obtain; there is no yoga higher than this.

items.question: What remarkable effect arises from step-by-step practice of this discipline?
premises: Practice is performed step by step
The practice is undertaken in this discipline
It produces great wonder
items.inference: Step-by-step practice in this discipline produces great wonder
items.plain_english: Indeed, when practiced step by step, it brings about great wonder.

rows.grounds: compound describing those for whom it is certain

items.question: For whom is there no doubt about the results of this practice?
premises: A result comes to be
There is no doubt in this matter
Some are devoted to constant practice
items.inference: For those devoted to constant practice, there is no doubt about the result
items.plain_english: There is no doubt about this for those devoted to constant practice.

items.question: What extraordinary power manifests during muttering focused on the image?
premises: Muttering occurs in relation to an image
It takes place in that context
Breaking of pots and stones occurs
items.inference: In that muttering upon the image, there is the power to break pots and stones
uncertainties: The exact form and meaning of pratimā+jalpanan is somewhat unclear
items.plain_english: In that muttering upon the image, pots and stones can be shattered.

items.question: Which major deities are included in the cosmic vision revealed by this practice?
premises: Brahma, Viṣṇu, Yama, and Indra are named
Varuṇa is named
Vāyu is named
items.inference: The vision includes Brahma, Viṣṇu, Yama, Indra, Varuṇa, and Vāyu
items.plain_english: Brahma, Viṣṇu, Yama, Indra, and also Varuṇa and Vāyu.

items.question: Which classes of semi-divine beings appear within the revealed cosmic vision?
premises: Gandharvas are included
Kinnaras, Yakṣas, and Nāgas are included
Vidyādharas are included
items.inference: The vision encompasses Gandharvas, Kinnaras, Yakṣas, Nāgas, and Vidyādharas
items.plain_english: Gandharvas, Kinnaras, Yakṣas, Nāgas, and Vidyādharas, O beloved.

items.question: How is the cosmic totality described in this vision of the universe?
premises: The cosmos is endowed with constellations and stars
The universe is encompassed as a whole
Both descriptions refer to the same cosmic vision
items.inference: The vision reveals the entire universe encompassed and filled with constellations and stars
items.plain_english: The universe, encompassed and endowed with constellations and stars.

items.question: What ability over one's own body arises from constant meditation?
premises: Constant meditation is practiced
One's own body can be shown
This can occur in many ways
items.inference: Through constant meditation, one can display one's own body in many ways
items.plain_english: Through constant meditation, he can display his own body in many ways.

items.question: What kind of accomplishment is granted through practice according to scripture?
premises: Accomplishment arises from practice
It is eightfold
It is enjoined by scripture
items.inference: Practice grants the eightfold accomplishment enjoined by scripture
items.plain_english: From practice comes the eightfold accomplishment enjoined by scripture.

premises: This Kaula teaching should be given to the worthy
It should not be given to just anyone
Discrimination in transmission is required
items.inference: This Kaula teaching must be given only to the worthy and not to anyone indiscriminately
items.plain_english: This Kaula teaching should be given to the worthy, not to just anyone.

It must be concealed always
One must be firmly resolved
